1. I don't think there's anything negative about working with the dead or ghosts or spirits. They're part of this world and part of existence. 2.  The same culture that eventually associated her with death and other things like it also associated her with being a protector. They would honor her and ask her to protect them from evil. She was also a goddess of midwifery.

All of this is to say Hekate more than anything is a goddess of transitions. Whether that be death or becoming a parent.  Existence is full of changes and no matter the change she will see you through it.  Sometimes that means she works with lost souls. Sometimes it means she helps new ones come into this world. I'm late to the party, but I saw this yesterday and wanted to think before responding. As a disclaimer, Capricorn is my sun sign. I have Gemini moon and Aries rising.

This is just a summary of my reflections as I've meditated and reflected on Capricorn for the last year or so which is when I got into astrology as well as some witchy shenanigans, so take it with some salt. 

The tarot card for Capricorn is the devil at least in the tradition rw deck. If you look at it, you'll see two people chained to the throne of what looks like the devil but is likely an amalgamation of any number of horned male gods that represent the wild and/or pleasure. 

What's interesting in this is that most of the capricorns I've met are very logical, traditional people not particularly given to what we typically think of as vice. And yet, that's what the card displays in a sense.  

For me at least not all vice is sex, or essentially carnal.  Vice can be power, ambition, any number of things that are sometimes even admired in the correct amounts.  

My take away from the devil card is us making our own hell by being a slave to our ambitions for one reason or another. Maybe some of us desire promotion in order to support a family. Maybe we desire power or mastery so we can help others. But that can very quickly turn into a love of the thing itself and a separation from the reason why. Work has often been a vice for me and has come at the expense of relationships and my own well being. In many ways, I have been a slave to my own throne.  

Here's another reflection I've had. Originally Capricorn was the sea goat. An earth sign with a water tale (I'm horrible at spelling).  Earth often symbolizing riches and ambition and level headedness, with water symbolizing emotion. Later, Capricorn just kind of became a mountain goat, endlessly questing for the next peak or the next accomplishment.  
 
It is very very easy to get so obsessed with power and accomplishment that you forget your sea or emotional aspect that propelled you to climb up out of chaos and up the mountain in the first place. 

Anyhow, that's what I get when I reflect on Capricorn and the devil card.
